contents.name: Proposition 11.4: far-kernel Hölder estimate and strict exponent test
contents.support: The local strategy evaluates the radial kernel integral and records (n-alpha)p' > n exactly when p < n/alpha.

contents.name: Footnote 88: identification with an inverse fractional Laplacian up to a constant
contents.reason: A Fourier symbol identity for the Riesz kernel is not needed for the Lp mapping theorem and would require a separate distributional kernel-transform proof.

sources.title: Larry Guth, Hardy–Littlewood–Sobolev Inequality, MIT OpenCourseWare lecture 30
sources.locator: Complete four-page lecture, introductory Proposition 0.1 and Theorem 0.2, §§1–3, printed pp. 1–3, plus OCW colophon p. 4. Guth writes |x|^{-gamma}; our potential order is alpha=n-gamma.

contents.name: Proposition 0.1: ball-indicator exponent and far-tail tests
§1 Lemma 1.1: finite Vitali covering
contents.reason: The maximal theorem is already supplied by the published measure-theory page, so this pair does not rebuild its finite covering lemma.

contents.name: §1 Lemma 1.2: ball-doubling estimate for finite unions
contents.reason: The finite-union doubling estimate is used in Guth's separate maximal-function proof and is not needed once the published maximal bound is imported.

contents.name: §2 Lemma 2.3: refined maximal superlevel estimate
contents.reason: The refined distributional estimate is part of Guth's maximal-operator derivation; the published strong maximal theorem already supplies this page.

contents.name: §3 Lemma 3.1: radial-average representation of the fractional kernel
contents.reason: The scaffold uses Williams's dyadic near-region decomposition, so Guth's alternative layer-cake representation is not needed as a separate claim.

contents.name: §3 Steps 2–3: small/large-radius bounds and maximal-function conclusion
contents.support: After gamma=n-alpha, Guth's two ball-average bounds give the same powers of Mf and ||f||p.

read_verification.method: Downloaded and extracted the complete four-page lecture PDF; inspected all three mathematical sections

sources.title: Eleonor Harboure, Spaces of Smooth Functions, §1 Fractional integration
sources.locator: §1 Fractional integration, printed pp. 1–7 (PDF pp. 2–8): definition, Theorems 1–4 and accompanying scaling, weak-endpoint, critical-endpoint and renormalisation arguments. Complete 19-page PDF fetched and the relevant pages inspected.

contents.name: §1 gradient representation and Sobolev motivation
contents.reason: The gradient representation is a Sobolev-embedding application; the assigned Fourier page proves the fractional integration operator bound itself.

contents.name: Remark following Theorem 1: dilation forces the target exponent
Weak-Lq definition and the radial weak/strong separation example
contents.support: The remark records the weak lower endpoint as orientation and avoids identifying it with strong Lq.

contents.name: Theorem 2: off-diagonal Marcinkiewicz interpolation
contents.reason: Harboure uses off-diagonal interpolation for an alternate HLS proof; this scaffold uses the published strong maximal estimate and Hedberg's pointwise inequality.

contents.name: Young convolution inequality reminder
contents.reason: The reminder supports Harboure's alternate weak-type proof; the assigned near/far lemma proves its bound with Hölder and centered maximal control.

contents.name: Proof of Theorem 1: weak (p,q) kernel split and interpolation
contents.support: Confirms the same strict range and kernel integrability conditions by an independent argument.

contents.name: Theorem 3: weak p=1 endpoint and failure of strong endpoint
Theorem 3 weak-type clause
contents.support: The weak estimate is recorded as an unproved orientation result, never consumed.

contents.name: BMO definition and Theorem 4 for compactly supported critical input
contents.support: The compact-support hypothesis and mean-oscillation target are retained explicitly.

contents.name: Remark after Theorem 4: renormalized general critical potential
contents.support: For general critical Lp input the far kernel is subtracted modulo constants; the raw integral is not claimed globally defined.
